{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Bulgaria|Cuisine of Bulgaria]]

This is a popular dish from Bulgaria and can be eaten on its own or as part of a main meal. This recipe will serve 2–3 people and can be prepared in less than 1 hour. It is adapted from [http://www.roesing.net/recipes/banitsa.html Ralitsa Roesing's kitchen].

==Ingredients==
* 2 packets [[cookbook:phyllo dough|phyllo dough]] (Bulgarian "fini kori" or phyllo from the frozen section)
* 200 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] [[Cookbook:Kashkaval|kashkaval]] cheese (or a mixture of [[cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar]] and [[cookbook:mozzarella|mozzarella]]), cut in small pieces
* 500 grams sirene or [[cookbook:Feta Cheese|feta cheese]], crumbled
* 7 [[Cookbook:Eggs|eggs]]
* 100 grams of [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Carbonated Water|soda water]]
* 1 cup [[cookbook:yogurt|yogurt]]

==Procedure==
# Mix 6 of the eggs, the grated butter, both cheeses, and the yogurt.
# In a buttered pan, lay a layer of the phyllo dough, spread a layer of the mixture, and continue alternating layers so that the phyllo and the mixture are finished about the same time. 
# Finish with a layer of phyllo dough on top.
# Cut the banitsa into serving pieces. 
# Mix the last egg with the soda water, and stir well.
# Pour the egg mixture over the banitsa, and make sure there are no pieces of the phyllo dough left dry.
# [[cookbook:Bake|Bake]] in a preheated [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] at 200 °C (390 °F) for 40 minutes, or until golden. Enjoy!

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* For spinach banitsa, substitute 3 of the eggs with ½ [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kilogram]] [[cookbook:spinach|spinach]], washed, cut and lightly fried (no more than 5 minutes).
* For green onion banitsa, substitute 3 of the eggs with 5–10 stalks of [[cookbook:green onion|green onion]] (about 1 cup chopped), lightly fried (no more than 10 minutes).
* Instead of piling the phyllo leaves on top of each other, you can just spread the mixture on the phyllo, top with a little soda and roll two of the leaves up around the mixture. The rolled phyllo is then aligned in a spiral in the pan. Sprinkle with some oil before baking.
